body:
feat(api): add nvim_win_resize()

Ref #6645

Problem:
When a window is resized it takes space from the window right/below first,
and only falls back to the window left/above when there is no more room.
Sometimes a user wants the space to come from a specific direction.

Solution:
Add nvim_win_resize(win, width, height, {anchor}) which resizes a window
with a choosable anchor edge, letting a window grow leftwards or upwards
by taking space from the window to the left or above first. The default
anchor reproduces nvim_win_set_width()/nvim_win_set_height().

comment_data.body:
the separate `win_setheight_win` and `win_setheight_win_dir` doesnt add much value. there aren't too many callers and requiring them to explicitly specify `start_from_next` isn't too bad.

for the the "width" variant
"cmdline" is the common way to say "command line". helps with grep
what is the intended meaning of `start_from_next`? if we can't think of a good name, it's better just to choose smething short, like `start_next` or `next` (just guessing)

we have `nvim_ui_try_resize`, `jobresize`, and `nvim_ui_try_resize_grid` all of which require both width+height.

probably makes sense for those to be required (positional) parameters for `nvim_win_resize`.

```
nvim_win_resize(Window win, Integer width, Integer height, Dict(win_resize) *opts, Error *err)
```

- `anchor` can stay "optional".
- for callers that only want to set `width`, we could treat `height=-1` as "don't care". and vice versa.

+/// Resize a window, choosing which edge stays anchored.

+/// The window first takes space from the non-anchored side (the window below or
+/// to the right by default), and only then from the anchored side. The "anchor"

+///

+/// @param opts  Optional parameters.
+///              - anchor: Edge that stays fixed while the opposite edge moves; the

+///                - "left" (default for width) or "right"
+///              - height: New height as a count of rows.
+///              - width: New width as a count of columns.

comment_regular_data.body:
@justinmk Regarding #6645, I haven't deprecated the old  `nvim_win_set_height/width()` yet. The new API is a superset. The old ones can be covered safely, do you think I should do it in this PR?

Also, currently, the API only supports specifying a single anchor even when both height and width are set.
We can either add parameters `height_anchor/width_anchor`, or we can support corner anchors such as "top-left".

I'm not sure which is preferable, or whether it's needed at all. Would appreciate your thoughts.

@justinmk  
Finally, with the help of Claude Code, I was able to get to the bottom of the failure.
The TLDR: it is a heap-overflow in `MsgPack::Raw`, which is used to parse the RPC. This PR happens to create the bytes that trigger it.


With the help of CC, I was able to:
- Conclude that the issue was not reproducible on my [local branch](https://github.com/XiaowenHu96/neovim/actions/runs/28658708411).
- Conclude that the issue IS reproducible with the latest head changes plus my changes [see here](https://github.com/XiaowenHu96/neovim/actions/runs/28664061766).

CC instrumented the CI with a coredump and was able to [see](https://github.com/XiaowenHu96/neovim/actions/runs/28664737855/job/85013585726) the program exit with SIGSEGV, with the backtrace landing inside msgpack-c, reached from:
```c
 #0  0x00007fc68167bfb6 in template_callback_array (o=0x55961936cc40, n=<optimized out>, u=0x55961936cc20) at deps/msgpack-c/src/unpack.c:207
#1  template_execute (ctx=0x55961936cc20, data=0x55961935cc10 "\001", len=<optimized out>, off=off@entry=0x5596189584c8) at deps/msgpack-c/include/msgpack/unpack_template.h:231
#2  0x00007fc68167d0d5 in msgpack_unpacker_execute (mpac=mpac@entry=0x5596189584b0) at deps/msgpack-c/src/unpack.c:507
#3  0x00007fc68167d26c in unpacker_next (result=0x7fff55b552f0, mpac=0x5596189584b0) at deps/msgpack-c/src/unpack.c:568
#4  msgpack_unpacker_next (mpac=0x5596189584b0, result=result@entry=0x7fff55b552f0) at deps/msgpack-c/src/unpack.c:590
#5  0x00007fc68167980b in XS_MsgPack__Raw__Unpacker_next (my_perl=<optimized out>, cv=<optimized out>) at ./xs/Unpacker.xs:62
#6  0x00005595e30681ea in ?? ()
#7  0x00005595e305d71e in Perl_runops_standard ()
#8  0x00005595e2f9bd3d in perl_run ()
#9  0x00005595e2f7165a in main ()
```

With further analysis, it found an overflow in:
```
// xs/Unpacker.xs
available = msgpack_unpacker_buffer_capacity(&self->unpacker);
if (size > available) {
    STRLEN extra = size - available;
    msgpack_unpacker_reserve_buffer(&self->unpacker, extra);  // reserves too little
}
memcpy(msgpack_unpacker_buffer(&self->unpacker), b, size);    // writes `size`
```

CC's explanation was:
> Whether the overflow is hit depends on the exact byte layout of the `nvim_get_api_info` blob the host parses at startup, and on how the OS chunks the pipe reads. This PR (plus master's ea0af59854, "preserve ArrayOf metadata") changes that blob, which is why the failure flip-flopped across my force-pushes and why it reproduces on CI but not locally — it's a pre-existing landmine, not something the window code does.

A suggested fix is:
```
  if (!msgpack_unpacker_reserve_buffer(&self->unpacker, size))
      croak("unpack: out of memory");
  memcpy(msgpack_unpacker_buffer(&self->unpacker), b, size);
```

With the patched msgpack module, I was able to pass oldtests [here](https://github.com/XiaowenHu96/neovim/actions/runs/28693966195).

During debugging, I also noticed that `Test_window_Cursor` / `Test_window_SetHeight` were skipped back in #28060. That PR has no comments or body, so I'm not sure if they were skipped for a similar reason.

So, if you agree with the explanation here, I propose another `fix(test)` commit to skip this test case.
I will also try to let the maintainer of p5-MsgPack-Raw to be aware of this issue.

> So, if you agree with the explanation here, I propose another `fix(test)` commit to skip this test case.
> I will also try to let the maintainer of p5-MsgPack-Raw to be aware of this issue.

SGTM, just be sure to include the details in the commit message.

Also added width/height = 0 support, to match the deprecated APIs (which clamp 0 to the minimum window size). 
Otherwise a size used to work will now fail on new API 
and I worry it might cause issue for downstream migration. 
Let me know if you think this is ok.
